reason: Safari WebDriver session could not be created because 'Allow remote automation' is off; enabling it would change Safari settings, which is out of scope for this verification.

safaridriver.command: safaridriver -p 4447 (started for this probe, then stopped)

value.message: Could not create a session: You must enable 'Allow remote automation' in the Developer section of Safari Settings to control Safari via WebDriver.

notDone: No Safari settings were changed and sudo was not used.
The Safari GUI was not opened deliberately; see sideEffect.
No WebKit-based substitute was run; every other result in this folder comes from Google Chrome 154 (Blink) and must not be read as Safari/WebKit coverage.
sideEffect: The POST /session attempt itself launched Safari.app (process start 00:12:16 AEDT, same second as the request) even though the session was refused. That Safari process was terminated (SIGTERM) right after; no Safari window was used and no setting was changed.
